stories.title: Tiafoe Stunned at Home — Atmane Upsets No. 6 Seed 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 at DC Open
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Terence Atmane (FRA) defeated hometown favorite Frances Tiafoe (USA, 6th seed) 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 in Round 1 of the Mubadala Citi DC Open on Monday July 27. It was Tiafoe's first opening-round loss in Washington since 2021. Tiafoe committed 25 unforced errors, 15 from his backhand. Atmane had lost to Tiafoe three previous times in 2026, including in Wimbledon Round 1. Also Monday: Taylor Fritz (3) def. Zizou Bergs 6-3, 6-4; Lorenzo Musetti (4) def. Matteo Arnaldi 6-0, 3-1 ret.; Kei Nishikori def. Marton Fucsovics 6-7(3), 6-3, 6-4. Tuesday headliner: Alex de Minaur (1, defending champion) vs. Stefanos Tsitsipas (wildcard).

stories.title: Jack Draper Withdraws from DC Open — Ranking Collapses from No. 4 to No. 147
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Jack Draper (GBR) withdrew from the DC Open before playing his first match, citing left arm bone bruising. The injury has been ongoing and wiped out his entire 2026 major season: Australian Open missed, Roland-Garros missed, Wimbledon missed. Draper received a wildcard for Washington but experienced increased soreness and pulled out. He was replaced by lucky loser Mackenzie McDonald. Draper's ATP ranking has collapsed from a career-high of No. 4 to No. 147. He is now targeting Montreal (wildcard needed) and Cincinnati ahead of the US Open.

stories.title: DC Open WTA — Fernandez Opens Title Defense; Eala vs. Zheng Headlines Tuesday

stories.title: Los Cabos ATP 250 — Norrie Ends Six-Match Drought; Cruz Hewitt Makes ATP Debut
stories.angle: NEW STORY — The Mifel Tennis Open by Telcel Oppo (ATP 250) opened Monday in Los Cabos, Mexico, running concurrently with the DC Open. Cameron Norrie (5th seed, GBR) defeated Aleksandar Kovacevic 6-4, 6-1 in 1 hour and 22 minutes, ending a six-match losing streak stretching back to April. The story of the day was Cruz Hewitt (AUS, 17 years old), son of Lleyton Hewitt, who qualified for the main draw via qualifying — with father Lleyton watching courtside. Cruz lost to Marcos Giron 6-3, 7-6(2) in Round 1 but became one of the youngest players to reach an ATP main draw this year. Top seed Jiri Lehecka leads the field; Denis Shapovalov (8th seed) is defending the title he won here in 2025, competing despite a shoulder injury sustained at Wimbledon. This is the tournament's 10th anniversary edition.
